text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 2.6% today after oil prices tumbled below $100 per barrel on reports that Trump signaled openness to talks with Iran, easing some of the geopolitical premium that had been pushing crude higher. The stock had spiked to $424.89 just three days earlier amid escalating Mideast tensions, but that rally has now reversed as traders price in a potential de-escalation scenario.

The move reflects the classic refiner's bind: while lower oil prices reduce their cost of crude, they also compress profit margins on refined products like gasoline and diesel. With refineries already running hot at 96.8% capacity and storage levels elevated across gasoline and diesel, cheaper oil doesn't immediately translate to better earnings if the market has already priced in a supply glut.
